title: Install the Missing Tool
description: The healthcheck script needs curl; refresh the package index and install it with apt.
scenario: A monitoring agent's healthcheck script fails because curl was never installed on this server. Your job is the standard Debian/Ubuntu drill: refresh the local package index with apt update, install curl, and verify the tool actually runs. This lab's container has network access so apt can reach the package archives.
symptoms: /usr/local/bin/healthcheck.sh fails immediately with 'curl: command not found'
No curl binary anywhere on the PATH
The local apt package index has never been refreshed on this box
mission: Refresh the package index, install curl, and verify that curl runs and reports a version.

hints.title: Index first, install second
hints.content: apt installs from its local index. If the index is stale or empty, `sudo apt-get update` refreshes it from the archives — always run it before installing.

hints.title: The -y flag
hints.content: `apt-get install -y curl` answers yes to the 'Do you want to continue?' prompt automatically — essential in scripts.

hints.title: Verify like an operator
hints.content: `command -v curl` prints the path if the tool is on the PATH and nothing (with a failing exit status) if it is not.

acceptance_criteria.description: curl is installed and on the PATH
curl runs and reports a version
the healthcheck script is still in place
